dimensions.question: Were consequential priors/unknowns identified and grounded before simulation?
Was an appropriate model selected and were its assumptions explicit?
Were materially distinct alternatives considered where useful?
Did simulation catch violations before mutation?
How closely did predicted observables match post-execution observations?
Did repair isolate failed dimensions without reopening passed state?
Were simulation, authorization, execution and verification kept distinct?
Did Veritas/receipt reflect only actual evidence?

comparisonDesign: For repeatable tasks compare baseline/direct execution versus kernel-governed execution on failure rate, retries, rollback incidence, time/cost, acceptance-pass rate and prediction error. Same task inputs/providers where feasible.
successRule: Promote claims only from observed comparative evidence. The kernel is useful if it measurably improves execution outcomes; no consciousness/imagination claim is inferred.
